title: Introduce onboarding compatibility linter and release-impact estimator
author: Priya Kapoor
release_notes: Adds an onboarding linter that enforces intake contract compatibility across hosted/dedicated/private deployments; introduces a lightweight release-impact estimator that auto-drafts changelog lines with performance and rollout guidance. No user-facing breaking changes.
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently see model intake manifests that pass schema validation but later fail in Dedicated or Private deployments due to subtle incompatibilities (quantization support, sequence-length assumptions, KV-cache sizing hints). This PR adds a focused compatibility linter + a release-impact estimator to reduce onboarding friction and automate initial changelog blurbs. The tools are intended to surface actionable remediation steps for SREs and platform owners and to seed the changelog with an impact paragraph that teams can edit before release.

What this PR does (summary): - Add onboard-compat-lint CLI and server-side hook that runs as part of intake validation. The linter checks: model config hardware affinity hints, quantization tags, tokenizer EOL/byte-level edge cases, max sequence vs memory budget heuristics, KV-cache compatibility markers, and model artifact packaging (sharded vs monolithic). - Add a release-impact estimator that consumes linter findings and a small local perf-profile (optional) to synthesize a suggested changelog entry: estimated QPS/latency delta, suggested rollout (canary size, fallback models), and recommended quantization/compile options. - Wire the linter into pre-submit checks in the intake service and the model registry onboarding pipeline; add a lightweight UI annotation to the model profile page showing the top 3 compatibility concerns.

Checklist: - [x] Linter core rules implemented and unit-tested - [x] Estimator heuristics implemented and documented - [x] Pre-submit hook added to intake pipeline - [x] Add API endpoint for UI annotation - [x] E2E smoke tests for a representative small/large model onboarding path - [x] Docs PR linking + short runbook attached

Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: introduce onboard-compat-lint package, rule runner, and basic rule set - 2d3e4f5: add estimator module and changelog templating engine - 3f4g5h6: integrate pre-submit hook + registry web annotation endpoint - 4h5i6j7: add unit tests and fixture models for quantization/kv-cache cases - 5j6k7l8: fix schema edge case found by CI (tokenizer metadata field optionality) - 6k7l8m9: polish messages and copy for release note drafts

Files changed (high-level): - packages/onboard-compat-lint/{index.ts, rules/*.ts, rules/README.md} - services/intake/hooks/preflight-check.ts - services/registry/api/compat-annotations.ts - ui/registry/components/CompatBadge.vue - tests/fixtures/{gpt-mini-quantized,bert-sharded}.tar.gz - tests/integration/onboard-compat.test.ts - docs/onboarding/compatibility-linter.md

Tests and CI: Initial CI run failed on a schema unit test (tokenizer metadata optionality) reported by tests/integration/onboard-compat.test.ts. The failure was addressed in commit 5j6k7l8 (made tokenizer.metadata optional in the validator and added a targeted unit test). After the fix CI passed on rerun; full suite green including lint, unit, and integration checks. A small perf regression was observed in a synthetic perf harness (3% median latency increase for tiny models when running the linter in preflight mode). To address this we changed the default preflight to run in asynchronous/opt-in scan mode for large payloads; the estimator can still be invoked with a flag to run the optional perf probe.

Review conversation (highlights): - Evan Li: "Nice rule set. Can we add an explicit rule for tokenizers that emit unknown-bytes on stream restarts? Also can the estimator annotate confidence scores for its latency/QPS numbers?" --> Author: "Added unknown-bytes rule and exposed estimator confidence (pct). See rules/tokenizer-unknown-bytes.ts and estimator confidence field in API response." - Marta Ruiz: "UI needs to avoid alarmist language by default; can we change red/yellow/green thresholds to mirror existing console thresholds?" --> Author: "Adjusted thresholds and added copy changes in CompatBadge.vue; thresholds are now configurable via registry feature flags." - Sanjay Patel: "If this flags models that require specialized GPU kernels, we need an automated fallback policy recommendation." --> Author: "Added fallback suggestions: recommended smaller variant, suggest quantize-to-fp16 or a fallback model alias if available. See estimator heuristics and produced changelog draft examples." - QA (Jessica Huang): "E2E onboarding smoke found an intermittent race when annotations are written back to the model profile after bake; added a retry + idempotency guard in compat-annotations.ts."

Backward compatibility and rollout: - Linter rules are additive; existing intake payloads will continue to pass when no issues are found. The pre-submit hook defaults to warning mode for accounts that have not opted into strict onboarding. - Default change: the UI will show annotations as a non-blocking banner; registry admins can flip strict mode via feature flag to make certain rules blocking. - No changes to runtime serving code paths were made in this PR.

Operational notes and runbook snippets included in docs/onboarding/compatibility-linter.md: quick remediation steps for quantization failures, how to interpret estimator confidence, how to set feature flags, and recommended canary sizes for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Security and privacy: the estimator optionally uploads a tiny perf sample when teams opt in; data is labeled with project id and retention follows registry retention policy. No secrets are stored by the linter.

Follow-ups (planned): - ENG-3421.1: add historical similarity lookup to surface prior onboarding fixes for similar models - ENG-3421.2: integrate estimator with rollout automation to propose A/B rollout percentages - PM-1189: product review session and UX polish for the CompatBadge expansion

Merge outcome: Approved by reviewers (Evan Li, Marta Ruiz, Sanjay Patel). CI passed after fix. Squash-merged into main on 2026-03-02 by Priya Kapoor.

Notes for release: include the generated impact paragraph by default in the model's release draft; provide a toggle for engineering teams to opt-out if they prefer manual notes. The change is low-risk to existing pipelines and should reduce onboarding rework for platform teams.
